status: Handoff batch complete: two guide-required cases added, evidence path made failure-tolerant, atomic publish implemented. Five-rank cross-device qualification remains pending the real five-GPU machine.

identity.provenance_note: The 16-case report (0cdd86bd) stays byte-identical history; this batch supersedes its qualification conclusions with the 18-case registry report below.

changes: case offset_addressing (guide 39.5 H06): interior slot at byte 72, 8-byte aligned but cache-line straddling, both directions, prefix/suffix arena guards
case multi_group_ordering (guide 39.6 P01/P02): deterministic reverse-order delays, max-index group finishes first, trap observation requires ready unpublished, 8 rounds
check_hip throws hip_error instead of exit(1); run_case records per-case failures and drains best effort
device setup failure keeps a device record with device_identity=fail and not_run handshake cases; teardown is null-tolerant
run_five_rank never aborts the process: HIP failures attributed by rank, best-effort drain and teardown, report always written

evidence publish via same-directory temp file + fsync + hard link; existing files and symlinks refused; no temp residue on any path
CLI rejects --output and --bench naming the same file before any GPU work

verification.config_test_coverage: 18-case registry, pattern determinism, strict JSON serialization, exclusive-write success/refusal/content-intact/no-residue

limits: Single-device results do not qualify five-rank cross-device behavior; run_five_rank has never executed on any machine.
Failure-tolerance paths are verified by code review, config tests and CLI negative checks, not by injecting HIP faults on real hardware.
Atomic publish does not claim crash durability of the directory entry; it guarantees a complete-or-absent file for a normally completing process.
Bench values are single-device observations and are not qualification gates.
